deletion_policy.description:
Whether Terraform will be prevented from destroying the instance. Defaults to "DELETE".
When a 'terraform destroy' or 'terraform apply' would delete the instance,
the command will fail if this field is set to "PREVENT" in Terraform state.
When set to "ABANDON", the command will remove the resource from Terraform
management without updating or deleting the resource in the API.
When set to "DELETE", deleting the resource is allowed.
deletion_policy.rationale: Controls whether the external VPN gateway can be destroyed via Terraform. The default (DELETE) allows unrestricted deletion, risking permanent loss of VPN connectivity and configuration. Setting it to PREVENT blocks destructive operations, acting as a safety guard against accidental or unauthorised deletion. Policy should require PREVENT for production VPN gateways to enforce the prevent-destructive-loss archetype.

description.description: An optional description of this resource.
description.rationale: A free-text description for human reference. It has no effect on the resource's security configuration.

labels.description:
Labels for the external VPN gateway resource.

**Note**: This field is non-authoritative, and will only manage the labels present in your configuration.
Please refer to the field 'effective_labels' for all of the labels present on the resource.
labels.rationale: Key/value metadata for organisation, billing, and filtering. Labels are cosmetic and informational, carrying no bearing on confidentiality, integrity, or access control.

name.description:
Name of the resource. Provided by the client when the resource is
created. The name must be 1-63 characters long, and comply with
RFC1035.  Specifically, the name must be 1-63 characters long and
match the regular expression '[a-z]([-a-z0-9]*[a-z0-9])?' which means
the first character must be a lowercase letter, and all following
characters must be a dash, lowercase letter, or digit, except the last
character, which cannot be a dash.
name.rationale: The resource identifier. We do not constrain resource names — naming conventions may aid governance but the name itself does not affect confidentiality, integrity, or access control.

project.description: The ID of the project in which the resource belongs. If it is not provided, the provider project is used.
project.rationale: Specifies the owning project. Project identifiers are non-security-relevant references at the resource level — project placement and IAM boundaries are governed at a higher organisational level.

redundancy_type.description: Indicates the redundancy type of this external VPN gateway Possible values: ["FOUR_IPS_REDUNDANCY", "SINGLE_IP_INTERNALLY_REDUNDANT", "TWO_IPS_REDUNDANCY"]
redundancy_type.rationale: Determines the redundancy configuration of the external VPN gateway. This is an architectural/availability choice left to teams, not a platform-level security control.

interface.description: A list of interfaces on this external VPN gateway.

interface.id.description:
The numeric ID for this interface. Allowed values are based on the redundancy type
of this external VPN gateway
* '0 - SINGLE_IP_INTERNALLY_REDUNDANT'
* '0, 1 - TWO_IPS_REDUNDANCY'
* '0, 1, 2, 3 - FOUR_IPS_REDUNDANCY'
interface.id.rationale: An internal numeric index identifying which interface slot within the gateway configuration. This is a structural identifier, not a security control — we do not constrain resource-internal numbering.

interface.ip_address.description:
IP address of the interface in the external VPN gateway.
Only IPv4 is supported. This IP address can be either from
your on-premise gateway or another Cloud provider's VPN gateway,
it cannot be an IP address from Google Compute Engine.
interface.ip_address.rationale: The IPv4 address of the external peer VPN gateway. External peer IP addresses are team-specific network endpoints that belong to external parties and cannot be generalised into an org-wide whitelist without knowledge of partner infrastructure. Constraining specific peer addresses would overreach into team-specific configurations.

interface.ipv6_address.description:
IPv6 address of the interface in the external VPN gateway. This IPv6
address can be either from your on-premise gateway or another Cloud
provider's VPN gateway, it cannot be an IP address from Google Compute
Engine. Must specify an IPv6 address (not IPV4-mapped) using any format
described in RFC 4291 (e.g. 2001:db8:0:0:2d9:51:0:0). The output format
is RFC 5952 format (e.g. 2001:db8::2d9:51:0:0).
interface.ipv6_address.rationale: The IPv6 address of the external peer VPN gateway. Same as interface.ip_address — peer addresses are team-specific network endpoints that cannot be generalised into platform-level policy without overreaching into team infrastructure.

params.description: Additional params passed with the request, but not persisted as part of resource payload

params.resource_manager_tags.description:
Resource manager tags to be bound to the ExternalVpnGateway. Tag keys and values have the
same definition as resource manager tags. Keys must be in the format tagKeys/{tag_key_id},
and values are in the format tagValues/456.
params.resource_manager_tags.rationale: Binds Resource Manager tags to the resource. Tags are team-specific resource metadata that cannot be generically mandated by platform policy without overreaching into team-specific taxonomy.
